en.title: Minimum Partitions to Keep After Redistributing Data
en.description:
Each partition has a capacity and a used amount, and data may be split into chunks and moved to other partitions. Find the minimum number of partitions that must be kept to hold all existing data; data in an original partition does not have to be moved as a whole.

This site independently compiled the standard I/O and editorial; supplements to missing source bounds and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n, the second line contains n capacities, and the third line contains n used amounts. The original had no numeric bounds; this site adds 1≤n≤200000, capacities 1..10^9, and 0≤used[i]≤capacity[i]. When the total usage is 0, this site explicitly outputs 0.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 2; 0; 1. Verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: The total used amount does not change; sort the capacities in descending order and take the shortest prefix whose total capacity reaches the total usage.
